isolated.notes: Omitting fork_turns forks full history and rejects model/effort overrides.

spawn.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: spawn_agent({task_name, message, fork_turns:"none"}) returned {"task_name":"/root/receipt_probe"}. The handle is that path, not a uuid or a threadId; it is the value every other collaboration call takes as target. A collaboration agent is not a Codex thread: set_thread_archived on the same path answered "No Codex thread found".

direction_update.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: exposed as send_message({target, message}). Delivers without starting a turn; not probed in this session.

idle_continuation.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: followup_task({target:"/root/receipt_probe", message}) started a new turn and returned an empty body; the reply arrived as a FINAL_ANSWER message. Keys are target/message, not thread_id/prompt — those belong to the separate thread surface.

wait.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: wait_agent({timeout_ms}) returned {"message":"Wait completed.","timed_out":false} for a pending mailbox update and {"message":"Wait timed out.","timed_out":true} when none remained. The schema permits up to 3600000 ms, but this host's own working rule forbids blocking longer than 60 s while a user is waiting, so plan the interactive ceiling and re-wait.

interrupt_turn.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: interrupt_agent({target}) returned {"previous_status":"running"} and the entry stayed in list_agents as "interrupted" — the runtime is not closed. It does free execution capacity: with three running children a fourth spawn failed with "collab spawn failed: agent thread limit reached", and after interrupting all three a new spawn succeeded. Capacity counts running turns, not entries.

close.reason: No close tool is exposed. interrupt_agent stops the turn and frees execution capacity but leaves the agent listed; set_thread_archived rejects a collaboration handle ("No Codex thread found"); no unsubscribe tool exists. A role can therefore be interrupted and replaced by a new spawn, but no call proves its runtime was released.
close.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: close_agent, thread/resume and thread/unsubscribe are all absent from the exposed surface; archiving a collaboration handle was refused.

observe.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: list_agents({}) returned {"agents":[{"agent_name","agent_status"}]}. Observed statuses are "running", "interrupted" and the object {"completed":"<last reply>"}. There is no "idle": record a completed object as completed, and never expect a bare string for it.

resume_closed.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: archiving with {archived:true} and restoring with {archived:false} both succeeded, and the restored thread completed a new turn and answered. That is a real resume, with two limits. It works only on the thread surface - a collaboration path handle is rejected - and only with a threadId you already hold, because list_threads cannot find these threads again. Archiving is not proven to release anything: the thread reported status "notLoaded", which is a status, not a capacity receipt.

task_create.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: target is nested, never flat ids. {"type":"projectless"} returned {threadId, projectlessOutputDirectory, hostId}; {"type":"project", projectId, environment:{type:"local"}} returned {threadId, hostId} and the thread ran. Get projectId from list_projects. WORKTREE WAS NOT ADDRESSABLE BY ANY ROUTE TRIED: environment {type:"worktree"} returned only {"clientThreadId":"client-new-thread:<uuid>","hostId"} and that value is rejected everywhere - wait_threads answers "No Codex thread found", read_thread answers "Invalid conversation", set_thread_archived the same, and the thread never appears in list_threads. The worktrees are really created (two detached-HEAD checkouts under ~/.codex/worktrees, and startingState {type:"branch", onMissing:"create-branch"} did create the branch), so a worktree task can be started and then neither driven, waited on, nor cleaned up through this surface. Do not plan worktree-bound tasks on it until a way to resolve clientThreadId into threadId is observed. Observed 2026-09-16, second round: a {type:"project", environment:{type:"local"}} thread is a usable role runtime. Its cwd is the project root, it reads repository files, it executes shell (latestToolMarker type commandExecution), it keeps context across turns, and a 96-second turn completed without being cut off. One caveat decides whether a role can run there at all: the thread shell activates the workspace toolchain, so the controller refused with RUNTIME_BUN_TOO_OLD 1.3.14 < 1.4.2 under the repository pin. Dispatch such a role with an absolute path to a satisfying Bun. Worktree creation remained unaddressable across every route tried: wait_threads and read_thread and set_thread_archived reject the provisional id, list_threads and list_archived_threads never showed the task, fork_thread and handoff_thread reject it as an invalid session id, get_handoff_status finds no operation, a retry after a minute changed nothing, and a child instructed to send its own id back never arrived. Those are nine failures, not a proof that no route exists: a mapping this session cannot see, or one the host adds later, would change the answer. Plan as if unaddressable, and revisit if the host publishes a way to resolve clientThreadId.

task_message.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: keys are threadId and prompt. It starts a turn and returns only {"threadId"} - the reply text is not in the response, and is read through wait_threads or read_thread. The collaboration surface uses target/message; the two are not interchangeable. Observed 2026-09-16: a threadId is not bound to the context that created it. Another collaboration child read the thread, sent it a message and waited on it successfully, so any role holding the id can address it.

task_wait.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: targets is an array of {threadId, hostId?, afterCursor?}. The result carries the new assistant text, so no separate read is needed: {wake:{reason:"turnCompleted",turnId,threadId}, polls:[{cursor,revision,changed,thread:{status:{type:"idle"}},latestTurn,latestAssistantMessage:{text}}]}. The cursor form is "<uuid>:<revision>"; passing the newest one back returns changed:false with latestAssistantMessage:null immediately rather than blocking to the timeout. timeoutMs is capped at 120000 - 3600000 was rejected with "Too big: expected number to be <=120000", so this is a different and much lower ceiling than wait_agent's. A read_thread cursor is a different type: passing one here is accepted but answers cursorReset:true, and passing a wait cursor to read_thread is rejected with "invalid cursor". Observed 2026-09-16: a turn longer than the wait ceiling is not lost. The first 60-second wait returned timedOut:true with the thread status "active" and latestTurn status "inProgress" carrying a "commentary" message; a second wait then delivered the completed turn with durationMs 96427. Short wait plus re-wait covers a long turn.

task_list.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: limit is the ONLY accepted key - cursor, cwd, searchTerm, archived, isPinned, sortKey and sortDirection were each rejected with "Unrecognized key". The earlier claim that a child thread can be recovered by filtering on cwd is false. Worse for recovery: none of the threads created in this session appeared in the list at all, and list_archived_threads did not show them either after archiving. Entries carry {id, kind, projectId, hostId, status, cwd, updatedAt, title, summary} with status among "active", "idle", "notLoaded". Treat a threadId as unrecoverable once lost.

wake_schedule.notes: Observed 2026-09-16: there is no prompt/interval form. Create takes mode:"create", kind:"cron"|"heartbeat", name, prompt and an RRULE string; a heartbeat adds destination:"thread" with targetThreadId, and returned {"automationId":"sdd-host-receipt-probe","mode":"create","status":"ACTIVE"}. It fired: the host delivered a heartbeat input into the target thread carrying automation_id, current_time_iso and the creation prompt. Delete is {id, mode:"delete"} and returned {"deleteStatus":"deleted","snapshot":{...}}. Unverified: the interval. The create receipt carries no timestamp, so the elapsed time between creating and firing cannot be computed from these receipts - one delivery is proof that a wake arrives, not that it arrives on the declared RRULE. Creating one is a persistent side effect that this host s approval review refused until the user authorized it explicitly, and an automation left ACTIVE keeps firing; treat scheduling as a user-authorized action and delete the probe.

limits.thread_quota_note: Observed 2026-09-16: five threads existed while three collaboration children ran, and a fourth child was still refused, so thread creation did not consume the collaboration allowance in that arrangement. That is one arrangement, not a proof of independent quotas. Twelve threads were then created in sequence without refusal; nothing measured how many were simultaneously active, so this is a lower bound on creations, not on concurrency, and the thread ceiling is unknown.
limits.concurrent_children_note: Observed 2026-09-16: a fourth concurrent child was refused with "collab spawn failed: agent thread limit reached" while three ran, and interrupting one let a new spawn through. The user reports far larger counts at other times - up to 47 children in a single thread - so this is not a ceiling anyone may plan against. The host manages child lifecycle itself and releases capacity on its own schedule. Treat a refusal as a fact about this moment: react to it, never precompute against a number. Any check that compares a planned role or shard count to a fixed concurrency figure would be a hard gate on an invented constant.

requires: Capacity is whatever the host allows at that moment; a refusal is the only signal and it cannot be predicted.
A role cannot be closed, only interrupted, so replacing one costs an interruption.

Observed 2026-09-16: create with target {type:"project", environment:{type:"local"}} - the thread then runs in the project root, reads repository files and executes shell. A projectless thread gets an output directory under Documents instead and is not a repository role.

Observed 2026-09-16: the thread shell activates the workspace toolchain, so the role runs the controller on whatever Bun the repository pins. That is the intended arrangement; configuration reports runningBun so a runtime-attributable failure is recognisable.
Observed 2026-09-16: a threadId is addressable from any context, so a Coordinator running as a collaboration child can drive thread-hosted roles.
Observed 2026-09-16: a turn longer than the wait ceiling is not lost - wait, then wait again from the returned cursor.
No delivery has been completed with thread-hosted roles; the mode is proven as a runtime, not as a delivery.

NOT WIRED: this controller does not build the nested target a create_thread call needs, and its continue and wait calls are not generated either. The mode records what a host can host, not a path the plan can drive today.
